subject: general
question: Rajveer has invested Rs. 16,000 at 10% p.a. for 1 year on compound interest, compounded half-yearly. The amount received by him will be:
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 16,000

Rate of interest (R) = 10% p.a.

Time (T) = 1 year

Interest is compounded half-yearly

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Formula: A = P (1 + (R)/(100n))^(nT)

Where,

P = Principal amount

R = Annual interest rate

n = Number of times interest is compounded per year

T = Time the money is invested for in years

A = Amount after time T

**Calculation:**

Here,

P = Rs. 16,000

R = 10%

n = 2 (since interest is compounded half-yearly)

T = 1 year

Substitute the values into the formula:

A = 16000 (1 + (10)/(100 × 2))⁽² × ¹⁾

⇒ A = 16000 (1 + (10)/(200))⁽²⁾

⇒ A = 16000 (1 + 0.05)⁽²⁾

⇒ A = 16000 (1.05)⁽²⁾

⇒ A = 16000 (1.1025)

⇒ A = 17640

**The amount received by Rajveer will be Rs. 17,640.**
